practices.practice: In serverless environments initialize the MongoClient outside the function handler so the single client and its pool are reused across warm invocations and use small pools (e.g., maxPoolSize 3–5, minPoolSize 0).

Prefer Microsoft Entra ID (OIDC) authentication with a token-callback (DefaultAzureCredential / managed identity) instead of long-lived DB passwords when possible, using the driver's OIDC callback interface to supply tokens.

practices.practice: For local development use the DocumentDB Gateway image (Mongo protocol on port 10260) and allow TLS relaxation (tlsAllowInvalidCertificates) only driven by environment variables and never defaulted in production code.
Prefer the provider's textSearch / $search full-text capability instead of the community `$text` index for production lexical search needs on Azure DocumentDB.
Limit the number of indexes per collection (keep a modest budget, e.g., 5–15 indexes) and regularly review index usage (`$indexStats`) to drop unused indexes that add write cost.
Percent-encode reserved characters in usernames/passwords before inserting them into the connection URI and do not commit credentials in source control.
practices.source_name: Tutorial: Connect a Node.js web app with Azure DocumentDB
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB quickstart Node.js connection string encode password

practices.practice: Enable diagnostic settings and slow-query logs and create alerts on CPU, memory, IOPS, storage, and connection saturation appropriate to your cluster tier for production monitoring.
Reuse a single MongoClient for the life of a Node.js process; do not create a new client per request.
practices.prior_belief: Use a single shared MongoClient per Node.js process, enable the unified topology, and set maxPoolSize (e.g. ?maxPoolSize=50) in the connection string rather than creating clients per request.

practices.practice: Always connect with TLS (tls=true) and do not disable certificate validation in production.
practices.prior_belief: Enforce TLS by using tls=true (or ssl=true) in the connection string and verify certificates (do not disable certificate validation).

practices.practice: Do not commit credentials into source control; use environment variables and prefer secrets stores (Key Vault) or managed identities for production secrets management.
practices.prior_belief: Never commit DB credentials; store the DocumentDB connection string/username/password in Azure Key Vault and load at runtime (or use environment variables populated from Key Vault), and keep .env.example with placeholders only.

practices.practice: Use least-privilege database identities (per-app users or Microsoft Entra RBAC) rather than admin/root credentials for application access.
practices.prior_belief: Create least-privilege database users: use a dedicated app user with only the minimum roles/privileges needed (read/write on the sample_retail_08 collections) rather than admin/root credentials.

practices.practice: Avoid building query strings by concatenation; use driver filter objects or parameterized queries so the driver can safely and efficiently apply indexes.
practices.prior_belief: Avoid string-building queries; use parameterized queries/driver APIs (filter objects) to prevent injection and ensure indexes are used (e.g., db.collection.find({ segmentId: segId })).
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Node.js

practices.practice: Create single-field indexes on fields frequently used in filters or sorts (e.g., segmentId, customerId, createdAt) before using the dataset.
practices.prior_belief: Create a scalar index on fields frequently filtered/sorted (e.g., segmentId, customerId, createdAt); for MongoDB API use createIndex({ segmentId: 1 }) before running lookups.

practices.practice: For vector search define a dedicated embedding field and create the provider-specified vector index (choose DiskANN / HNSW / IVF based on scale), and tune build/search parameters to match recall/latency goals.
practices.prior_belief: For vector search, define a dedicated embedding field (e.g., embeddings: [Float]) and create the provider-specified vector index (HNSW/IVF) with explicit parameters (e.g., index type HNSW, M=16, efConstruction=200) appropriate for your recall/latency needs.

practices.practice: Normalize embeddings and record the embedding model and dimensionality alongside the vectors; reject or pad vectors of the wrong dimension on write.
practices.prior_belief: Normalize and fix embedding dimensionality on write (reject or pad vectors with wrong dimension) and optionally store L2-normalized vectors if you plan to use dot-product for cosine similarity.

practices.practice: Use partial or sparse indexes for optional large fields (like embeddings) so only documents with those fields are indexed to avoid index bloat.
practices.prior_belief: Use partial or sparse indexes for optional large fields (like embeddings) so only documents that contain embeddings are indexed, preventing index bloat: createIndex({ embeddings: 1 }, { sparse: true }) or provider equivalent.

practices.practice: Implement retry logic for transient errors and 429 rate-limits with exponential backoff and honor Retry-After when provided.
practices.prior_belief: Implement retry logic that handles transient network errors and 429 (rate limiting) responses with exponential backoff, honoring the Retry-After header when present.

practices.practice: Azure DocumentDB uses compute tiers and per-shard IOPS/throughput characteristics rather than Cosmos DB-style RU accounting; monitor CPU/memory/IOPS and scale the compute/storage tier and alerts accordingly.
practices.prior_belief: Monitor request units / consumed throughput and configure autoscale or increase provisioned throughput for the sample_retail_08 database/collections to accommodate vector search and LLM-generation bursts; add alerts on RU consumption.

practices.practice: Keep documents well under the 16 MB BSON document limit and store large binary attachments in Blob storage referenced from documents.
practices.prior_belief: Keep documents well under the MongoDB 16MB document limit; store large attachments (images, logs) in Azure Blob Storage and reference them from documents rather than embedding large binary blobs.

practices.practice: Avoid large skip offsets for pagination; prefer keyset (range-based) pagination using a stable sort key (e.g., createdAt + _id bookmark) for efficient paging.
practices.prior_belief: When doing pagination avoid large skip offsets; use range-based pagination or a stable sort key (e.g., createdAt + _id bookmark) to page through results efficiently.

practices.practice: Create required indexes before seeding or significant reads, and verify indexes at deployment time (listIndexes/listIndexes check) in your provisioning/seed scripts.
practices.prior_belief: Create indexes required by any query patterns before seeding/using the dataset (run createIndex in seed/provision script) and verify index existence with listIndexes as part of deployment validation.

practices.practice: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral documents (createIndex with expireAfterSeconds) to automatically expire old campaign drafts or staging documents.
practices.prior_belief: Use TTL indexes for ephemeral campaign drafts or staging documents (e.g., createIndex({ expireAt: 1 }, { expireAfterSeconds: 0 })) to automatically expire old campaign drafts.

practices.practice: Design writeConcern and readPreference intentionally for cross-replica durability or latency needs, but verify Azure DocumentDB's default mapping and supported features first.
practices.prior_belief: Set an appropriate writeConcern (and readPreference) for the workload: majority writeConcern if you need cross-replica durability; otherwise accept acknowledged writes for reduced latency—explicitly set in driver options.
practices.how_found: Azure DocumentDB writeConcern readPreference; Azure DocumentDB writeConcern support

practices.practice: Make writes idempotent or use upsert (e.g., replaceOne / updateOne with upsert: true) so retries do not create duplicates.
practices.prior_belief: Use idempotent writes or an upsert pattern (e.g., updateOne(filter, { $set: doc }, { upsert: true })) for campaign document writes so retries do not create duplicates.

practices.practice: Restrict network access to clusters with firewall rules, Private Link (private endpoints) or VNet integration and avoid exposing production cluster endpoints publicly.
practices.prior_belief: Restrict network access to the cluster using firewall rules, VNet integration, or private endpoints; do not expose the DocumentDB/MongoDB endpoint publicly to the internet for production workloads.
practices.source_name: Quickstart: Use Azure DocumentDB with MongoDB driver for Node.js

practices.practice: Enable slow-query logging and use explain('executionStats') / indexStats to detect COLLSCANs and add appropriate indexes to avoid collection scans.
practices.prior_belief: Instrument and log slow queries and index usage (use explain() / query plan tools) and address any queries that do collection scans by adding appropriate indexes.

practices.practice: Avoid sending raw PII to LLMs or retaining it in logs; redact or minimize PII in prompts and encrypt or limit sensitive fields at rest.
practices.prior_belief: Do not include raw PII in prompts or logs; redact or hash personally-identifiable fields before sending to LLMs and when storing generated drafts include only the minimal required customer attributes (or encrypt sensitive fields at rest).
practices.how_found: azure documentdb pii lLM redaction; documentdb privacy logging pii

practices.practice: Pre-create vector indexes and wait for their build/ready state before running similarity queries to avoid missing or inconsistent recall results.
practices.prior_belief: Pre-create any vector indexes and wait for the index build to complete before running similarity queries; include an index-building and verification step in your seed/provisioning script.

practices.practice: Use projection to fetch only needed fields (partial projection) when building prompts or assembling context to reduce bandwidth, I/O and cost.
practices.prior_belief: Use partial or sparse indexes for optional large fields (like embeddings) so only documents that contain embeddings are indexed, preventing index bloat: createIndex({ embeddings: 1 }, { sparse: true }) or provider equivalent.

practices.practice: Implement application-level retries for transient faults but avoid retrying non-idempotent multi-document transactions unless you can guarantee idempotency or use a deduplication token.
practices.prior_belief: Enable and test application-level retries for transient failures but avoid retrying non-idempotent multi-document transactions unless you can guarantee idempotency or use an application-level dedup token.
practices.how_found: resilience to transient faults azure documentdb retries guidance

practices.practice: Include provisioning and verification scripts that create collections, desired indexes, and perform a short sample query (listCollections/listIndexes) as part of deployment.
practices.prior_belief: Include a provisioning script that creates collections with the intended throughput/indexes and a verification script that calls listCollections/listIndexes and a short sample query to confirm connectivity and permissions.

practices.practice: Never log or persist raw connection strings or SAS tokens; use Key Vault references or managed identities and rotate credentials regularly.
practices.prior_belief: Don’t log or persist the raw DocumentDB connection string or SAS tokens; if you must persist connection metadata use Key Vault references or managed identity, and rotate credentials regularly.

notes: I inspected the app (src/client.js, src/seed.js, src/generate.js). The code follows many recommended patterns (MongoClient singleton, TLS in example URI, env-based secrets, index creation in seed, upserts for segments, projection could be added for prompt fields). The installed domain skills (documentdb-*) provided concrete, actionable best practices for connection pooling, security, indexing, vector search, monitoring, local development and query optimization; Microsoft Learn quickstarts complemented these with connection-string and auth examples. The only clear contradiction was K11 (RUs): Azure DocumentDB uses compute/IOPS/tiers rather than a Cosmos-style RU accounting, so the RU-focused prior belief does not map to this product.
